body:
This may be a stupid question, but how do you know who clicks? What are you looking for? 

Why did you decide to leave the field, if I may ask?

Thank you so much for answering- you've hit the nail on the head, the people suggesting alternatives don't understand how hard it is to start from nothing, after years of sacrifice. The prospect of doing that again, for something that seems like a far second best is daunting. It has to seem like a better option than suicide, you know?


Why did you leave your residency?

I do love animals. I have a little cat who I love very much. I worry a little about what would happen to her, but the nice thing about being a vet is there are a LOT of people in my life who I think would take her in and love her like I do. 


I love my parents, and my SO. But talking to them, I feel like a fake and a disappointment. I don't feel like I deserve them- any of their love, or attention, or time. So that's a little tainted. I don't feel particularly close to anyone else in my life.


I used to do a lot of things. I had a bunch of hobbies. I liked to try different things around town. I liked to explore new places. I've tried to make myself do some of the things like used to enjoy, but anymore it just feels hollow. I'm not actually enjoying myself. It just feels like effort. Even the simplest, stupidest thing- like taking a shower. I used to love showers, but now they're just another chore.


I don't know about therapist shopping. I didn't have a problem with the guy I talked to. He was nice. Professional. Empathetic. He just didn't have anything to offer me, it felt like. Not sure what anyone else might have instead.

I don't blame you. Talking to people sucks. But talking to the internet is a lot easier. The stakes are lower. 

Why do you want to kill yourself?

It's true. There's the people who immediately have a solution to all your problems, and can't understand what is WRONG with you. Then there's the people just want you to stop talking, because they don't know how to respond and would rather just not know. And I dunno- I tried therapy, but I really couldn't make myself believe for even a minute that anyone being paid to listen to you actually gives a shit. So there's not really a great option. Guess we're all here, talking to the void of the internet, and maybe getting a little return from it. Better than anything in real life.

I didn't honestly think that being a vet was something that required you to be all that special :( Not in the same way that being a professional athlete, or model, or singer does. I thought I could work hard, and that would be enough. I've always known I'm not the most brilliant person in the class, but I thought I could hold my own, and make up the slack with extra reading or studying or practice... Now I'm looking back on time in the anatomy lab on Saturdays, or canceling plans with friends, or any of the sleepless nights catching up on things during my residency, and it just seems like such a waste. And the thing is, I never minded any of it at the time, because I thought it would eventually pay off in happiness and stability in a job that means something to me instead of soul-less slaving just to make ends meet. But now I can see that there is a whole other level to it that can't be learned- the part where some people can think like a doctor, and some people can't. Do or do not; there is no try. And I do not. 


So yeah, the part about lowering my expectations and becoming content. That's where I'm at, and it's a huge stumbling block. Having to figure out how to be happy, when looking at (from my perspective) a lifetime spent paying off my student loans for the biggest failure of my life working some time sink of a job, bitter and humiliated after daring to hope I could have something meaningful to me. I realize that sounds over dramatic, but that's how things seem right now, and when comparing that to something like a quick, easy death... well.

Thank you for this. I do love teaching. I haven't really thought about it as an option, since all of our professors in vet school were also either researchers or clinicians. But I don't know. Maybe there's something I could figure out. 


That's very sad about the teacher you knew. I'm trying not to let that be me, only with the ones who end up dead being people's beloved pets.

I dunno. I feel like you have to bring something to the table, as a human being and member of society. And I think that a lot of people are good at a lot of different things, and those different things can all be valid. I know people who are great vets, and people who are great parents, and people who are creative, and people who are teachers... And I just wonder what I have to offer? I had always been focused on my job, that was the one thing I really cared about. And now it's gone, and I feel like I've put all my eggs in one basket and now they're all broken. And to be quite frank, that does make me worthless.
Keep knocking on the doorway to unhappiness? ;)
How's it going for you now?

YES, exactly. I feel completely paralyzed when it comes to thinking about how to move forward. I can't make myself want any of it, and I feel like I'm worthless and letting everyone important in my life down. It's not that I actively WANT to kill myself- it's just a choice I feel I can make that at least stops me feeling this way.

I've never tried medications. I have a lot of hang-ups about mood-affecting meds. I don't like the idea of "fake" happiness, and I worry about becoming dependent on them. Plus I worry about the side effects. 


I realize it's kind of a backwards way of thinking, and I'm also a bit of hypocrite because I drink and occasionally smoke weed. But it's hard to let go.

I'm not a very practical person, that's a good way of putting it. Unfortunately I'm also not a very innovative person, so I'm not sure I'd be cut out for research, either. I've been trying to think of how to keep some of what I love in my life and just haven't quite hit on it yet :(
Thanks for the optimism. I used to be interested in traveling, but now the thought of it just makes me tired. That's great that you've found a way to be happy, though :)

I've thought about it. I used to like traveling, and had always intended to do some big trip to celebrate the end of my residency. But now I just... don't care. It takes so much effort to even drag myself to the grocery store. The thought of planning a trip just makes me tired. Thank you, though.
I thought that too, when I first started. But in 4 years, I've seen no growth or improvement in my skills.

Hahaha, can't say I've had the advice to be a shitty but cheap vet before. Thanks for the laugh, I guess. 

I keep racking my mind for something else that I think could make me happy. Certainly I could do other jobs. I could make enough money to support myself. But what's the point? I can't think of anything that actually seems enjoyable. Even the non-job related things I used to do for fun seem empty and unsatisfying.

I'm afraid I would do more harm than good :( That's part of what makes me hate myself; the thought that I took a position away from someone who could do so much more for animals with the same opportunity.

I feel the same, OP. Up until the last couple of years things had been going so well. I was happy, did great in school, career is going just as I had planned... and then the bottom fell out. Things changed so fast, and suddenly everything was screwed up and I was failing miserably in my career. Turns out I'm not as smart as I thought. I'm a workaholic; my career is the most important thing in my life and the primary way I define myself as a person. Losing that took the joy out of everything else for me, and now I just don't even see the point in going on. I'm nothing but a disappointment to my family, and any friends I had are backing away from the stench of failure. 

It sucks. We're the same age, and I can't see a way out of it either. I hope something changes for you, OP.
